text:
Alex DeBrincat is the top scorer on a slumping team, and the Detroit Free Press framed his week exactly that way: "Alex DeBrincat on pressure as No. 1 scorer, Red Wings slumping." He has two goals and no assists in his last ten games, and 17 points in 23 overall.

The cold spell is part luck, part not. His own chances have held up fairly well (3.2 expected goals on his shots over the ten games, against 4.0 usual), and he's shooting 9.6% against a league norm of 13.4%. But the chances with him on the ice have thinned (12.1 on-ice expected goals against 14.3), so it isn't only the finishing. For the season he has 8 goals on 9.1 expected.

The play-driving hasn't gone anywhere. Detroit takes 56.1% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, 10.2 points better than without him, and Evolving-Hockey had him sixth of 401 forwards last season, against competition in the 92nd percentile. For the winger from Farmington Hills, playing for his hometown team, the thing to watch is whether the looks from in front of the net come back.
